title: VPC preflight kubelet-version skew + operator post-upgrade watchdog and hotfix
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers running Private/VPC deployments reported failed operator upgrades over the weekend after applying operator Helm chart v2.4.0 -> v2.4.1. Symptoms included: post-upgrade controller loops, mutating/admission webhook timeouts, and in some clusters nodes flapping NotReady. Customers A and B escalated to SEs with production impact (reduced serving capacity, transient 503s).

Investigation and root cause hypothesis:
- Preflight validation did not detect kubelet/node agent version skew. We observed kubelet versions 1.23.x on affected nodes while the operator post-upgrade webhook asserts feature gates that rely on 1.24+ behaviour. This caused webhook cache invalidation to fail and webhook probes to time out (observed 10-15s timeouts).
- Helm post-upgrade hook (post-upgrade:apply-migrations) assumes the operator CRD reconciliation will succeed in a single attempt; when webhook cache invalidation fails the hook times out and leaves partial state (CRs created but not reconciled).
- There was an unrelated config encoding change introduced in v2.4.0 that migrated an internal Secret from raw to base64-with-prefix; clusters with automation that re-applied Secrets (GitOps) drifted back to raw format and triggered reconciliation failures.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Provided per-customer runbook to manually rollback operator to v2.4.0 (helm rollback <release> 1) and to restart operator pod after cleaning the post-upgrade Job. Applied kubelet taint removal and restarted nodeagent on a small subset to recover CV.
- Released a short-lived patch script (rbx/operator/rollback-watchdog.sh) which removes the stuck post-upgrade Job and sets an annotation to skip post-upgrade hooks; used for emergency remediation for 3 customers.

Work to be done (this ticket):
1) Add preflight kubelet version gate to the installer/upgrade controller and surface a readable error to the Helm preflight (fail fast if kubelet < 1.24).
2) Harden Helm post-upgrade flow: make post-upgrade hooks idempotent and re-entrant, add exponential retry with backoff for controller readiness checks, and ensure Helm waits on a stable operator health endpoint rather than a single reconciliation checkpoint.
3) Implement operator watchdog: a small in-cluster controller that detects stuck post-upgrade Jobs (long-running > 5m) and either retries reconcile or marks the cluster for safe rollback and notifies SRE/SE.
4) Add config-drift detector for Secret schema changes and a migration helper that safely migrates raw -> prefixed-base64 secrets during upgrade.
5) Prepare a 2.4.1-hotfix branch and release (operator-2.4.1-hotfix) containing backports and a migration job.
6) Update customer-facing runbook and support KB with explicit manual remediation steps and rollback commands.

Acceptance criteria:
- Installer/upgrade command fails with clear message when kubelet < 1.24 and points to remediation steps.
- Post-upgrade hook logic retries on webhook timeouts and does not leave partial CR state after a failed attempt.
- Watchdog auto-detects stuck Jobs and either remediates or creates a ticket in the ops queue with full diagnostics.
- Migration helper transforms drifted Secrets safely and is idempotent.
- 2.4.1-hotfix released and validated in our staging clusters and at least two customer clusters without regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Day 0: Merge preflight gate + watchdog + migration helper into a hotfix branch. Deploy to staging (smoke test: upgrade 3 clusters with kubelet 1.24 and 1.25).
- Day 1: Run controlled canary on two low-risk customer clusters (customer opt-in). Monitor operator health, webhook latency, and Helm job durations.
- Day 2: Open rollout to remaining Private customers with scheduled maintenance windows. Communicate to SEs and update support runbook.

Notes and trade-offs:
- Blocking upgrades for kubelet < 1.24 will break some customers that lag on OS updates; we need to offer a supported path: (a) explicit skip flag with acceptance of risk (not recommended) or (b) automated nodeagent upgrade path coordinated with customer.
- Making hooks fully idempotent increases complexity; initial approach is to add retries and a watchdog. A subsequent release should refactor hooks to be truly re-entrant.

Links and artifacts are included below for follow-up and handoff.
